bear.narrative: The CIF PJBB is not renewed beyond 29 October 2029, the spread stays at the H1 2026 trough through the remaining term, and the bank refuses to roll the facilities, so the group has to close a capital deficiency of more than a trillion rupiah. A rights issue at the market price would be massively dilutive: a Rp300bn raise at Rp37 adds about 8.1bn shares, roughly doubling the count. The model carries the earnings path and a 300bp higher required return; the dilution and the loss of the post-2029 book push equity value toward zero.

bull.narrative: The PJBB is renewed, Newcastle eases toward the deck's long-run marker, the PLN spread widens back toward the FY2025 level, and the market closes part of the governance and liquidity discount as the bank debt is repaid and the capital deficiency narrows. Volumes run at the top of the contract's +/-20% band rather than above it.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is the midpoint between the company's 2,000.0kt delivery target (the PJBB contract quantity) and the 2,174.0kt actually shipped in FY2025, which beat the internal budget of 1,900.0kt by 14.4% [S2, F3, F4, F73, F74]; half-year revenue was 2.2% below the prior year [S4]. FY2027E-FY2029E hold 2% nominal as the five-year contract rolls and the remaining book is re-priced [S3]. Long-run growth is the house macro deck's 2.5% Indonesian inflation midpoint, not a real-growth assumption.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2025 gross margin of 20.4% is the margin at FY2025 input prices: coal purchases were Rp1,062.8bn of the Rp1,483.3bn cost of revenue and freight Rp388.1bn [S3]. The coal link then squeezes it when Newcastle trades above its FY2025 average, which is what H1 2026 shows (14.0% gross margin) [S4].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Purchased coal of Rp1,062.8bn was 71.6% of FY2025 cost of revenue; the rest is freight, coal consumed by the Pangkalan Bun plant, depreciation and handling [S3].

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Calibrated on the H1 2026 actual: gross margin fell from 20.4% in FY2025 to 14.0% while the coal deck's Newcastle average rose from 108.4 to roughly 129 US$/t, so about 41% of the purchase-cost move reached the PLN selling price [S4]. That move is the total gross-margin move and therefore already embeds the first-half freight and fuel squeeze, which is why the separate Brent link is set to zero (link2_share) rather than counted twice.

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: share of COGS exposed
assumptions.basis: Set to zero to avoid a double count: H1 2026 freight-in of Rp388.1bn annualised is a large part of the margin move from 20.4% to 14.0%, and link1_pass is calibrated on that total move [S3, S4]. A separate Brent link on top added about 0.9pp of FY2026E and 0.5pp of FY2027E gross-margin drag that the actual already contains.

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Retained at the template default for completeness; with link2_share at zero it has no effect. Freight is recovered in the delivered CIF price but the tariff resets with the annual contract [S3].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 general and administrative expenses of Rp62.5bn were 3.35% of revenue and H1 2026 ran at 3.61%; we hold the last audited actual [S3, S4].

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 total depreciation of Rp17.0bn (fixed assets Rp16.6bn plus right-of-use amortisation) was 0.91% of revenue; taken from the notes, because the data pack carries only a fraction of the charge [S3].

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Capital expenditure was Rp0.7bn in FY2025, 0.04% of revenue; there are no material capital commitments and the plant is maintained, not expanded [S2, S3].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: At 30 June 2026 current assets less cash were Rp464.4bn against current liabilities less current debt of Rp1,404.2bn, an operating working capital of about Rp939.8bn, or -50.4% of FY2025 revenue, close to the -49.3% held [S4, F77, F78]. Only the annual change in this float enters the cash flow; its capped level (-49.3% of revenue, not a rising percentage) does not add to enterprise value. The Rp379.9bn of refundable security deposits inside the float are separately deducted in the bridge as debt-like [S4, F76].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: FY2025 tax expense of Rp52.3bn on pre-tax profit of Rp247.3bn is a 21.1% effective rate; held at the last actual [S3].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: FY2025 interest and finance charges of Rp57.7bn on opening interest-bearing debt of Rp463.3bn is 12.4%; the Bank Sinarmas term loan fell to 10.5% in February 2026 and the Sinar Mas Multifinance facility carries 14%, so the blended rate is held [S3, S4].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Interest income of Rp0.6bn on opening cash of Rp143.1bn is a 0.4% yield; the cash sits in low-yielding current accounts, most of it at Bank Sinarmas [S3].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: H1 2026 net repayment was Rp31.0bn, almost all the Bank Sinarmas term loan, which matures in November 2027; the model continues the amortisation and clears the bank facility by FY2028, while the Sinar Mas Multifinance facility runs to April 2029 [S3, S4].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minority interests took Rp0.4bn of the Rp195.0bn FY2025 net profit, 0.2%; the remaining mining subsidiary (AJP) is 51.3%-held but has no operations [S3].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: The stated policy is a 40% payout, but the board paid nothing for FY2025 because of the capital deficiency, the 2012 dividend of Rp16.3bn is still unpaid, and the bank facility covenants restrict dividends; a zero payout is the most likely path [S3].

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: The house macro deck's long-run Indonesian inflation midpoint of 2.5% (Bank Indonesia target band), applied to a business whose terminal cash flow is in rupiah and whose volumes are contracted rather than resource-limited [S3, S4]. There is no real-growth assumption after the 2029 contract: the terminal value carries nominal escalation only, consistent with flat Indonesian thermal-coal demand in the deck's long-run view [S3].

challenges.challenge: The headline market-cap figure is a unit error repeated twice. fund record uses {{mkt.mcap_idr|idrbn}}; mkt.mcap_idr is 331,385,364,622 IDR (Rp331.4bn), but the formatter appends "bn" without dividing, so the summary and thesis bullet 3 print "IDR331,385,364,622.0bn" - 1e9 times the true market cap and about 1e9 times FY2025 EBITDA, immediately next to the "1.4x FY2025 EBITDA" claim. The true multiple (mult.FY2025A.ev_ebitda 1.369) is computed correctly, so the error is presentation, not model; but a reader cannot verify the valuation anchor as printed.
challenges.answer: Accepted. mkt.mcap_idr is denominated in rupiah, so |idrbn appended "bn" without dividing. Every market-cap and ADTV placeholder now uses |idrb, which divides by 1e9: the market cap renders IDR331.4bn in the summary, thesis and section 2, and no |idrbn placeholder remains in fund record.

challenges.section: Investment summary / 3. Financial analysis and forecasts
challenges.challenge: FY2025 parent equity is mis-cited. S3's balance sheet shows equity attributable to owners of the parent of (1,037,579,477) at 31 December 2025, with total capital deficiency 1,064,284,851; the engine's equity line agrees (FY2025A -1,037.579). The report prints "parent equity of IDR-940.8bn [S3]" in the summary, thesis bullet 3, section 1 and section 3. -940.8bn is the 30 June 2026 figure (F51/S4). The sentence is also arithmetically inconsistent with its own numbers: total assets 891.4 less total liabilities 1,955.6 is -1,064.2, and FY2025 minorities were -26.7bn, so -940.8 plus -26.7 is -967.5, not -1,064.3. A reader who opens S3 finds a different number.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Added FY2025 and FY2024 parent-equity facts F68/F69 from S3. Every FY2025 reference now prints -1,037.6bn [S3, F68]; -940.8bn is kept only for 30 June 2026 [S4, F51]. The arithmetic now ties: total assets 891.4bn less total liabilities 1,955.6bn less minorities of -26.7bn gives parent equity of -1,037.6bn, matching the engine line.

challenges.challenge: The DCF runs 10 years plus a terminal value, but the only dated coal sale agreement in the filings is the PJBB effective 30 October 2024 to 29 October 2029 (S4 p.71), about three years from the valuation date. Discounting the model's own rows, the PV of FY2030-FY2035 FCFF plus the terminal value is 2,266bn of the 2,984bn EV (76%); only 24% of the value sits inside the dated contract. Section 4 calls the terminal value "not extreme for a business with a stable contract book" without stating the expiry or arguing renewal, and the going-concern note's "five-year mid-term contract" is undated.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The only dated coal-sale agreement is the PLN CIF PJBB effective 30 October 2024 to 29 October 2029, for 2,000,000 mt (+/-20%) a year [S4 Note 37, F73]. The DCF horizon is cut to four years (FY2026E-FY2029E), so the explicit cash flows stop at contract end; the terminal value is 71% of EV and is supported by the renewal record (PJBBs since January 2011, restated June 2019, CIF contract April 2022, amendments August 2024 and January 2026, with the consortium term extending if the PJBB continues). Renewal is the base case and non-renewal is the nil bear case, so the report shows both values.

challenges.challenge: The negative working capital is the model's biggest funding assumption and its reversal is the report's named stress, but the balance-sheet driver is never quantified. At 30 June 2026 trade payables are Rp956.8bn, up from 777.0bn at December 2025; Rp595.2bn is owed to PT Borneo Indobara alone, up from 454.3bn (S4 Note 14). That is about 200 days of COGS and roughly six months of BI's H1 purchases of 600.2bn. The report says only that "suppliers ... run well ahead" and "if a large supplier demands its deposit back"; it never states the payable balance, the BI share, or that a reset to 30-day terms from BI alone needs about Rp496bn, 1.5x market cap.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Added facts F70 (trade payables 956.8bn), F71 (Borneo Indobara 595.2bn) and F81 (Borneo Indobara H1 purchases 600.2bn) and quantified the exposure in section 5: the payable is about two hundred days of cost of revenue and six months of Borneo Indobara purchases; a reset to thirty-day terms from that supplier alone would call on roughly five-sixths of the payable, close to one and a half times the market capitalisation. No undrawn facility funds it; the consortium relationship and the PJBB are the only protection, and both are why the bear case carries a 30% weight.

challenges.challenge: Trade receivables rose to Rp327.6bn from Rp114.6bn (+185.7%) between December 2025 and June 2026 while revenue fell 2.2% (S4 p.4); receivable days go from about 22 to 58. Cash received from customers was 810.6bn, 79.2% of H1 revenue, so it is not yet a collection collapse - but this is exactly the EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS divergence test (receivables growing more than 1.5x revenue growth), and the report mentions the 327.6bn balance only in passing ("part of it factored with recourse") without explaining the jump or its relation to the 258.6bn with-recourse facility.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Note 5 shows gross receivables of 922.1bn less a 594.5bn allowance, so the net 327.6bn rise from 114.6bn is PLN billing timing: billed PLN Indonesia Power and Nusantara Power receivables appeared in the half and unbilled PLN balances rose, while the with-recourse factoring liability of 258.6bn is flat, so it is not a factoring presentation. Cash received from customers was 810.6bn, or 79.2% of H1 revenue. Added facts F72/F75/F83/F84; the report shows the gross, allowance and net balances, the cash-collection ratio and the receivable-day move, and the forecast does not extrapolate the spike.

challenges.challenge: The report says "we treat a contract loss as the central bear case, not a remote tail", but the bear scenario only adds -3pp to revenue growth, -3pp to gross margin and +2pp to WACC (fund record scenarios.bear). It does not model loss of the PLN book, a bank acceleration, a debt-for-equity swap or a rights issue - although a capital deficiency of 1,064bn makes some capital action likely, and a Rp300bn raise at Rp37 would add 8.1bn shares (+90% dilution). All three scenarios value the equity at 8-21x the price, so the probability-weighted 508 cannot reflect the downside the report says it fears.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The bear is rebuilt as a harsher, sourced scenario: no renewal after October 2029, the H1 spread trough persisting, a failed refinancing, a three-hundred-basis-point higher required return and the capital deficiency closed at a distressed price. It values at nil and carries a 30% probability. The bull mirrors the same drivers within the contract's +20% volume band, and the asymmetry is justified in qc_justifications. The report also states that a Rp300bn rights issue at Rp37 would add about 8.1bn shares, roughly doubling the count, and that the modelled bear is a floor rather than the worst case. The weighted target is Rp193 and the rating BUY.

challenges.challenge: The forecast takes the 2,000kt FY2026 delivery target at face value (revenue -2%, then +2%/yr), but the same annual report says 2025 shipments of 2,174.0kt beat the internal budget of 1,900.0kt by 14.4% (S2 p.38). The report cites the target only as evidence of a guided-down volume ("the direction matters") and never tests a repeat beat: at the modelled price/tonne the 2025 actual volume would add about 8.7% of revenue and Rp17-20bn of gross profit, roughly 10-13% of FY2026E EBITDA. No bull case touches volume.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Section 1 states the 2025 shipments of 2,174.0kt against the 1,900.0kt internal budget, a 14.4% beat [S2 p.35, F3/F74/F86], and the FY2026 base is the midpoint between the 2,000kt contract quantity and the FY2025 actual rather than the face-value target; revenue growth FY2026E is -0.5% rather than -2%. The bull case runs at a repeat of the FY2025 volume within the contract band, and the assumptions basis records the volume and margin linkage.

challenges.challenge: The remaining AJP concession is valued at zero ("optionality ... worth something close to nothing"). S8 shows 95.35Mt of resources including 60.57Mt measured; the April 2026 SRI sale valued 73.5Mt at Rp50bn cash (S4 Note 39), which at the same Rp680/t implies about Rp65bn for AJP, or Rp7/share (2% of target). The method card says value everything the company owns and never zero a development asset without a sourced basis.
challenges.answer: Accepted. AJP is no longer valued at zero. The bridge carries 95.35Mt of resources at the per-tonne value implied by the April 2026 SRI sale (73.5Mt for Rp50bn, or about Rp680/t), half-weighted at probability 0.5 because there is no mine plan, permit or funding commitment. That is about Rp65bn gross, or Rp3.6 per share. Section 1 and section 4 explain the treatment and its haircut.

challenges.challenge: The terminal gross margin fades from 21.13% in FY2029 to 16.81% in FY2035 (engine gross_margin line) although the base input margin is held at 20.4% and the coal deck's long-run newc is flat at 105 with USD escalation. The fade comes from the COGS link comparing an escalating forecast price with a fixed FY2025 base price (108.4), not from any sourced cost driver. On FY2035 revenue of 2,405bn the gap is about 104bn of gross profit, roughly 25% of terminal FCFF; correcting the outer years lifts the DCF about 15% (about Rp50/share).
challenges.answer: Accepted. The fade was an artefact of running FY2030E-FY2035E with a fixed FY2025 cost base against an escalating forecast price. The horizon is now four years to the October 2029 contract end, so those rows are gone; the terminal value is built from FY2029E FCFF and escalates price and cost together at 2.5% nominal, so the terminal gross margin is held rather than faded. The assumptions basis states the nominal-consistency rule and no sourced cost decline remains.

challenges.challenge: WACC uses kd_pre_tax 9.45% (rf 7.45% plus the house default spread) against the company's actual borrowing: the Bank Sinarmas term loan is 10.5% after the February 2026 cut (S4 Note 42), the Sinar Mas / AB Sinar Mas factoring is 14% with recourse (S4 Note 19), and the analyst's own cost_of_debt input is 12.4% (FY2025 interest 57.7 on opening debt 463.3). At 12.4% the WACC is about 13.7% (from 12.56%), which cuts the DCF about 11% (about Rp37/share). No company-specific premium is added despite negative equity and a going-concern paragraph.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Added a 3.43pp COE premium. Of that, 2.43pp aligns the engine's macro-deck debt cost with CNKO's actual blended borrowing cost: the Bank Sinarmas term loan is 10.5% after the February 2026 cut [S4 Note 15, F87], the Sinar Mas with-recourse factoring is 14% [F65], and the analyst's input is 12.4%. The remaining 1.0pp is a company-specific charge for negative equity and the going-concern paragraph [S3]. WACC rises to 14.2% and the DCF and target are shown at that rate; the coe_premium_note documents the arithmetic.

challenges.challenge: The EV/EBITDA cross-check applies 17.25x to FY2025A EBITDA of 334.8bn - the peak year - and carries 20% weight. fund record peers show the median is computed from ten trailing multiples spread from 3.04x (DWGL) to 46.50x (SGER); the closest distribution/trading names are 3.0-7.4x (DWGL 3.04, MAHA 5.36, BBRM 6.68, TPMA 7.44), and the 17.25x median is set by 21.6-46.5x logistics/asset names (RMKE, MBSS, TCPI, BESS, SGER). The cross-check contributes 0.2 x (643.5 - 331.9) = Rp62 of the Rp394 blended today value (Rp74 of the Rp465 base one-year value). The multiple is also cited [S0], which is CNKO's own Yahoo page and cannot support a peer median.
challenges.answer: Accepted. The EV/EBITDA weight is set to zero and the cross-check is removed from the target; the 17.25x median and the peak-on-peak multiple are no longer used. Section 4 states why: the engine strikes the multiple on FY2025A peak EBITDA of 334.8bn and the peer set's trailing multiples are too dispersed (about three times to more than forty times) to form a comparable median. P/BV is also zero on negative book, so the DCF carries 100% of the weight.

challenges.challenge: Terminal growth of 4.0% is above the macro deck's long-run IDR inflation of 2.5% and applies in perpetuity to a coal-volume business that section 6 itself calls structurally exposed to the energy transition. The report's only justification is "the standard rupiah rate applies". At g = 3.0% the DCF is about 10% lower (Rp300/share from Rp332); at 2.5% about 13% lower. With a five-year contract and a declining coal burn in Java, 4% nominal (1.5% real) growth is an unsourced optimistic input.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Terminal growth is cut from 4.0% to 2.5%, the house macro deck's long-run Indonesian inflation midpoint, with no real growth after the contract. The assumption basis and section 4 state the source and that the terminal value carries nominal escalation only, consistent with flat long-run thermal-coal demand; the sensitivity table shows the effect of moving g.

challenges.section: 3. Financial analysis and forecasts / 7. Catalysts and monitoring
challenges.challenge: FY2026E is a fresh 12-month run from FY2025, not H1 actual plus H2 forecast. FY2026E EBITDA 149.4 less H1-26 EBITDA 110.4 (EBIT 106.3 + D&A 4.1, S4 p.7) leaves H2 EBITDA 39.0; FY2026E gross profit 193.9 less H1 143.2 over H2 revenue 802.9 gives a 6.3% H2 gross margin against 14.0% in H1. The report never discloses this, and section 7 says "a gross margin above the first-half level would validate the base case" - which would actually be a large beat against a 6.3% H2 base. The pass-through formula at H2's newc (about 145) implies about 8-9%, so the model is also about 1.5-2pp below its own link.
challenges.answer: Accepted. FY2026E is now H1 actual plus an implied H2 at the deck's second-half price: revenue of 1,854bn, gross profit of 214bn and a blended gross margin of 11.5%; the implied H2 margin is about 8.5% against H1's 14.0%, which reconciles to the newc path and the 41% pass-through rather than the old 6.3%. The old result was itself too low because the separate Brent link double-counted the H1 freight squeeze; link2_share is now zero. Section 3 shows the reconciliation and section 7's signpost now refers to the implied second-half margin, not the first-half level.

challenges.challenge: Operating working capital is held at -49.28% of revenue in every year and grown at 4% in perpetuity, so the model books a permanent, growing cash inflow from supplier and customer float. At June 2026 the float includes Rp379.9bn of refundable security deposits (286.7 long-term + 93.3 short-term, S4 Note 20) and Rp956.8bn of trade payables. Section 4 says the bridge treats the deposits as operating liabilities; if a buyer had to honour them, equity value falls by Rp379.9bn, about Rp42/share (13% of the DCF). No cap, decay or funding cost is applied to the float.
challenges.answer: Accepted. NWC is capped at -49.3% of revenue rather than a rising percentage, and only its annual change enters FCFF, so the float does not grow faster than the business. The June-2026 actual reconciles: current assets of 802.7bn less cash against current liabilities of 1,525.4bn less current debt gives about -939.8bn, or -50.4% of FY2025 revenue, close to the -49.3% held. The 379.9bn of refundable security deposits are deducted as a debt-like claim in the bridge, and section 4 states that the float is supplier credit at zero interest with rollover risk, not permanent equity.

challenges.challenge: link1_pass of 41% is calibrated on the total FY2025-to-H1-2026 gross-margin move (20.4% to 14.0%) against newc (108.4 to 129), which already embeds the H1-26 freight cost. The model then applies a separate Brent link on top: FY2026E Brent of 96.0 vs FY2025A 68.1 (+41%, oil deck) adds (1 - 0.6) x 0.07 x 41% = 1.15% of COGS, about 0.9pp of revenue margin, and FY2027E (+23%) about 0.5pp. That is a double count of the fuel squeeze and understates the base-case margin.
challenges.answer: Accepted. link2_share is set to zero. link1_pass is calibrated on the total FY2025-to-H1 gross-margin move, which already embeds the first-half freight and fuel squeeze; a separate Brent link on top added about 0.9pp of FY2026E and 0.5pp of FY2027E margin drag that the actual already contains. The assumption basis and section 3 document the decomposition, and FY2026E gross margin rises to 11.5%, reconciling with H1 actual plus H2.

challenges.challenge: The coal price references are attributed to the wrong sources. Section 2 says "Newcastle spot was US$150.3 ... while the HBA reference was US$126.8 [S6]"; S6 (investor.id, 4,758 chars) contains Newcastle October 150.15 / November 150.35 / December 152.65 and no HBA line at all, and 126.81 is the coal deck's HBA spot sourced to S1/S14 in fund record Sections 3 and 7 similarly cite [S3, S6] for the deck's FY2025A 108.4, FY2026E 137.0 and FY2027E 118.0; S3 is the audited financial statements and S6 carries no such path. The numbers are the reviewed deck's, but a reader checking the citations finds nothing.
challenges.answer: Accepted. Every coal-price citation is corrected: Newcastle spot now cites S6, the high-GAR HBA cites the newly registered S10 (DDTCNews on Kepmen 401.K/MB.01/MEM.B/2026), and the forward path is named as the house coal deck (World Bank Pink Sheet annual averages and Newcastle contract prints) rather than a false [S3, S6]. FY2022 revenue and EBIT now cite [S0, S3]; the peer-median citation is gone with the cross-check; and the special-monitoring status is now stated as unverifiable from the September release list [S9]. Section 2 also adds the DMO grade point (5,575 kcal AD / 4,290 AR against a 6,322 GAR cap) and the macro tilt.

missing_bull_case.note: Four sourced upsides are outside every priced case. (1) The model takes the 2,000kt FY2026 delivery target at face value (revenue -2%, then +2%/yr), but the same annual report says 2025 shipments of 2,174.0kt beat the internal budget of 1,900.0kt by 14.4% (S2 p.38); a repeat beat is in neither base nor bull. (2) AJP holds 95.35Mt of resources including 60.57Mt measured (S8) and is valued at zero; the April 2026 SRI sale valued 73.5Mt at Rp50bn cash (S4 Note 39), which at the same Rp680/t implies about Rp65bn for AJP, Rp7/share. (3) The S6 DMO tightening redirects off-grid supply to the grid, which should support CNKO's PLN volumes, but is framed only as a constraint. (4) Net debt at the FY2026E trough is 61.9bn against 149.4bn EBITDA (0.41x) and cash almost covers debt, a resilience point the going-concern discussion omits; H1-26 CFO of 102.2bn (S4 p.9) also contradicts the "cash is not real" tone. C7, C8.

missing_bear_case.note: Three material downsides are absent or unquantified. (1) Trade payables are 956.8bn at June 2026, up 180bn in six months, of which 595.2bn is owed to PT Borneo Indobara (S4 Note 14) - about 200 days of COGS and roughly six months of BI purchases; the negative working capital is supplier credit, not a stable float, and a reset to 30-day terms needs about 496bn from BI alone, 1.5x market cap. (2) Trade receivables jumped to 327.6bn from 114.6bn (+186%) while revenue fell 2.2%, lifting receivable days from 22 to 58 (S4 p.4); this is the EARNINGS_QUALITY divergence flag and is not discussed. (3) Section 5 calls a contract loss "the central bear case", but the bear only adds -3pp to revenue growth; a rights issue or debt-for-equity swap to close the 1,064bn capital deficiency would be highly dilutive at Rp37 and is in no scenario. C4, C5, C6.

assumption_realism.note: FY2026E does not reconcile with the reported half-year. FY2026E EBITDA of 149.4 against H1-26 EBITDA of 110.4 (EBIT 106.3 + D&A 4.1, S4 p.7) implies H2 EBITDA of 39.0, and FY2026E gross profit 193.9 less H1 143.2 over H2 revenue 802.9 implies a 6.3% H2 gross margin against 14.0% in H1. The report never shows this, and section 7 says a 9M gross margin above H1 would "validate the base case" - which would actually be a large beat against the modelled 6.3%. The base should be H1 actual plus a sourced H2 forecast. Separately, operating working capital is held at -49.3% of revenue every year and grown at 4% in perpetuity, and the terminal gross margin fades with no driver. C13, C14, C9.

evidence_and_citations.note: Spot-checks verify: F26/F50 debt reconciliations (381.8 = 122.5 bank + 259.0 factoring + 0.2 consumer; 350.5 = 91.8 + 258.6 + 0.1, S4 Note 39); F61/F62 capital deficiency 1,064.3/783.1 (S3 p.81); F53 receivables 327.6/114.6 (S4 p.4); F64/F65 258.6 at 14% (S4 Note 19); F66 336.6 at Bank Sinarmas; F4 2,000kt target (S2 p.38); F57 US$70 cap (S6); S3 auditor/BDO and the material-uncertainty going-concern paragraph; the 30 April 2029 factoring maturity. Failures: (a) FY2025 parent equity is -1,037.6bn in S3; the report prints -940.8bn citing [S3], which is the 30 June 2026 figure (F51/S4), repeated in summary, thesis bullet 3, section 1 and section 3; (b) the market-cap placeholder renders as IDR331,385,364,622.0bn (1e9x too high) in the summary and thesis; (c) HBA 126.81 and the deck coal path are cited [S3, S6] but S6 contains no HBA line and S3 no coal price - they are fund record values (S1/S14/S19/S23); (d) FY2022 revenue/EBIT cited [S3, S7] although neither filing covers FY2022; (e) the peer multiple 17.25 is cited [S0] (CNKO's own Yahoo page), not the peers' packs; (f) CNKO's special-monitoring/notation status is inferred from absence from the S9 release list and is never sourced. C1, C2, C16.

valuation_method_fit.note: The DCF is the right primary method, but the horizon and terminal treatment are not justified: the only dated coal sale agreement in the filings is the PJBB effective 30 October 2024 to 29 October 2029 (S4 p.71), yet the model runs ten years plus a terminal value. About 76% of the DCF enterprise value (PV 2,266 of 2,984) falls after October 2029, and renewal is neither sourced nor stress-tested. The EV/EBITDA check capitalises FY2025A peak EBITDA 334.8 at a 17.25x median drawn from 3.0-46.5x (distribution/trading subset 3.0-7.4x), a peak-on-peak cross-check. The WACC debt cost is 9.45% against the Bank Sinarmas 10.5% (S4 Note 42), the 14% Sinar Mas factoring (Note 19) and the analyst's own 12.4% input; at 12.4% WACC is about 13.7% and the DCF about 11% lower. Terminal growth of 4% exceeds the 2.5% long-run IDR inflation in the macro deck. C3, C10, C11, C12.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose is disciplined and the model is transparent, but every scenario is 8-21x the price (bear 302, base 465, bull 799 vs 37), so the 861% return is an artifact of a probability set that cannot reach the market. Presenting "the bear case is still above the price" as a finding rather than as a warning that the DCF is miscalibrated is the main tone failure. "The market is pricing the loss of the PLN book" is asserted from the reverse DCF alone, with no evidence of market expectations. "We do not put a probability on" a bank refusal while assigning bear 25% is inconsistent. Credit: the sources, the debt restatement, the negative-equity framing and the refusal to use P/BV are honest and well argued. C6, C12.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Reads the coal deck correctly (newc FY2027E 118.0, FY2028E 110.0, lt 105; FY2026E 137.0 matches the Q1 122.3/Q2 135.4 prints), but the house card says Indonesian coal realisation keys off HBA/ICI while the model uses Newcastle only; the deck carries a reviewed HBA FY2027E of 112.0 and ICI4 (needs_source) that are never tested. The DMO cap is described as limiting pass-through, but CNKO's realised FY2025 coal price is about US$52/t (Rp857k/t at the 16,448 deck FX) against a US$70/t cap set for 6,322 GAR; the grade and whether the cap binds are not stated (AJP's CV is 5,575 AD/4,290 AR, S8). The macro tilt (thermal coal NEUTRAL, balance-of-payments CAUTIOUS) and the complex beta required by VAL_COMMODITY_CYCLICAL section 1 are absent. C16.

conservatism_audit.note: Below last actual / unsourced: terminal gross margin 16.8% in FY2035 vs 21.1% in FY2029 against a 20.4% base input, from nominal escalation of the coal price against a fixed FY2025 base (about 15% of DCF); FY2026 volume anchored to the 2,000kt target vs 2,174kt actual and a 14.4% budget beat; AJP valued at zero; link1_pass 41% calibrated on the total H1 margin move and then a separate Brent link applied, double-counting about 0.9pp of FY2026 freight squeeze. Optimistic: WACC debt cost 9.45% vs 10.5-14%; terminal g 4% vs 2.5%; EV/EBITDA 20% weight on a 17.25x non-comparable median; -49.3% working capital in perpetuity with 4% growth; no company-specific premium despite negative equity. Shocks are mirrored (+/-3pp growth, +/-3pp margin, -/+2pp WACC), base 50%, and the 30% illiquidity discount is the house maximum. C9, C10, C11, C12, C14, C15.

calibration.note: The QC gate passes and all five BLOCK/WARN flags are justified with sources that say what they claim: the FY+1 margin gap is the deck's 137.0 vs FY2025 108.4 at 41% pass-through; the debt restatements reconcile to Note 39 (381.8 and 350.5); the extreme call names the EBITDA, capex and net-debt drivers; the weight change is explained by negative book. But FY+1 (FY2026E) is a forecast run from FY2025 rather than the last actual half-year, so the model's own FY2026E implies H2 EBITDA of 39.0 against H1 110.4 and a 6.3% H2 gross margin against H1 14.0%; the gate cannot see this because it compares only FY2025A to FY2026E. Rebuild FY2026E as H1 actual + H2E and re-run. C13.

signoff.notes: APPROVED — leave at signoff for the Director to publish. The round-1 FIX on the security deposits is answered by the primary source and needs no model change. S4 Note 20 carries Uang jaminan of Rp93.282bn current and Rp286.660bn non-current on the LIABILITIES side: they are deposits RECEIVED from PT Berau Coal Energy and PT Sinergi Laksana Bara Mas under coal-sale/transport agreements [S4 Note 20], so treating the Rp379.942bn as a debt-like claim a buyer must honour is correct, and it is not inside the Rp12.2bn net debt (bank loans plus the Sinar Mas factoring less cash). The only deposit ASSET is S4 Note 11, Rp307,820 (building-lease and health-insurance deposit), immaterial. The QC finding's "omitted deposit asset" premise reads Note 11 against the Note 20 liability; close the FIX next round by citing S4 Note 20 and F37/F38/F76 and stating Note 11's Rp0.3m — do not add Rp379.9bn back to the bridge. Rating and target otherwise reproduce: FY2026E is H1 actual plus an implied H2 at the deck's price, the four-year horizon ends with the 29-Oct-2029 PJBB [F73], and the +420% return is the company's own ~1x LTM EBITDA with net debt of Rp12.2bn, not a shared-input tilt. Batch check clean.

bias.note: Neutral, both directions checked. The base is anchored to the reviewed deck (newc FY2026E 137.0, FY2027E 118.0, S19/S23) and to last-actual ratios (opex 3.35%, capex 0.04%, NWC -49.3%, tax 21.1%); FY2026E is H1 actual plus an H2 at the deck's price and recomputes to a 9.1% EBITDA margin, so the -8.9pp calibration gap is sourced, not a slicer. The scenario shocks hit the same three drivers (growth, margin, WACC) with base 50%. Conservative offsets: maximum 30% illiquidity discount, 30% nil bear, half-weighted AJP and Rp379.9bn deposits deducted; the main omission running the other way is the un-added Rp307.8bn refundable deposit asset (Q4), so the base is not net-tilted. The 71.1% terminal share rests on the sourced PJBB renewal record (renewed since 2011, amended Jan-2026) and is stressed to nil in the bear.

findings.finding: The investment-summary sentence carrying the house coal deck's forward path (newc US$118.0 FY2027E and US$110.0 FY2028E) still ends [S6], but S6 contains only the spot prints (150.15/150.35/152.65) and no forward path; section 2 correctly names the deck. This is the residue of C16 on the one sentence that was not re-cited.

The extreme-call justification states "FCFF is about 90% of EBITDA". The model's FCFF/EBITDA is 77.9% FY2026E, 86.4% FY2027E, 85.3% FY2028E, 84.8% FY2029E and 65.1% FY2025A, so ~85% is right for the forecast years and 90% overstates. The DCF uses the actual FCFF; no value change.

post_bs_review opens "after the 31 December 2025 balance sheet", but the valuation uses the 30 June 2026 balance sheet (net debt 12.2, cash 338.3). The search window does run to November 2026 (S9/S10) and no post-June material event is identified, so the substance is intact; the reference date is stale.

The bridge deducts Rp379.9bn of refundable deposits received (S4 Note 20) but does not add the Rp307.8bn refundable security-deposit asset (S4 Note 11, building lease and health-insurance deposit) that sits outside operating NWC because it is non-current. The net deposit position is about -Rp72.1bn, not -Rp379.9bn; the asymmetric treatment is worth roughly Rp34/share (14% of the DCF value) and is not disclosed.

The AJP bridge item applies the SRI price per tonne to 100% of AJP's 95.35Mt, but AJP is 51.30%-held (S3 p.13); the attributable value is about Rp16.6bn rather than the Rp32.4bn carried, a ~Rp1.8/share (0.7%) overstatement.

IDX special-monitoring/notation status remains unverified: the report correctly stops inferring it from absence from the S9 release list but does not source the actual board/notation, which EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS makes a first-order investability gate for a negative-equity name.

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves -8.9pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: FY2026E EBITDA margin falls from 18.0% to 9.1% because the coal deck's FY2026E Newcastle price of 137.0 US$/t is about 26% above the FY2025A average of 108.4 and only roughly 41% of the purchase-cost increase passes into the PLN tariff; the H1 2026 actual gross margin of 14.0% and the 2,000kt contract target already show the squeeze, and FY2026E is H1 actual plus the implied H2 at the deck's second-half price [S3, S4, F4, F43, F79].

flags.message: a.gross_margin: bear -0.08 vs bull 0.04 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The bear assumes the H1 2026 spread trough persists and the capital deficiency is resolved at a distressed price, while the bull only recovers toward the FY2025 20.4% gross margin at the deck's long-run coal price [S3, S4, F9]; a -8pp slide is achievable from the 20.4% base but a +4pp gain is already a full spread recovery.

flags.message: a.revenue_growth: bear -0.1 vs bull 0.05 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The asymmetry is deliberate and sourced: the PLN CIF PJBB covers 2,000,000 mt (+/-20%) a year to 29 October 2029 (F73), so the bull's volume upside is capped near 2,400kt while the bear can lose the whole post-2029 book and faces a capital deficiency of 1,064.3bn [S3, S4, F61, F73]; the -10pp bear and +5pp bull bracket those bounds.

flags.message: val.wacc: bear 0.03 vs bull -0.02 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The bear adds a 300bp required return for a failed refinancing and a going-concern outcome [S3, F61], while the bull removes only 200bp of the base's 343bp company premium; the base already carries the debt-cost alignment and the going-concern premium, so the bull cannot re-rate below the capital-market cost [S3, S4].

flags.message: debt FY2025A restated at 2.12x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The pack's FY2025 debt of 180.4bn captures only part of the financing liabilities. The audited financing-liability reconciliation in Note 40 totals 381.8bn: bank loans 122.5, Sinar Mas recourse factoring 259.0 and consumer finance 0.2 (F26). The factoring balance is debt-like because it is a with-recourse facility priced at 14% [S3, S4].

flags.message: balance-sheet debt restated at 2.35x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The pack's 30 June 2026 debt of 149.4bn omits the Sinar Mas Multifinance recourse factoring line. The H1 2026 Note 40 reconciliation totals 350.5bn: bank loans 91.8 and other financial liabilities 258.6, the latter a 14% with-recourse factoring facility running to April 2029 [S4].

flags.message: expected return +420%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Three sourced drivers produce the return. First, the 2.0-2.2Mt PLN distribution book earned 334.8bn EBITDA and 233.7bn operating cash flow in FY2025 against a market capitalisation of 331.4bn, about 1x LTM EBITDA [S3, F1, F3]. Second, capex is 0.04% of revenue and the fleet is leased, so FCFF is about 90% of EBITDA [S3, F24]. Third, the SRI sale left net debt at only 12.2bn, so nearly all enterprise value is equity, and the six-month operating cash flow of 102.2bn shows the business still funds itself [S4, F49, F50, F85]. The reverse DCF shows today's price implies FY2027E revenue growth of -12.3%, i.e. permanent loss of the PLN contract [S3, S4].

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.5, 'ev_ebitda': 0.3, 'pbv': 0.2}
flags.justification: PBV carries no weight because parent equity is negative (-940.8bn at June 2026 and -1,037.6bn at December 2025), so book value cannot anchor value. The EV/EBITDA cross-check is removed to a zero weight because the engine strikes it on FY2025A peak EBITDA and the peer set spans 3.0x-46.5x, a non-comparable distribution; the DCF, which models the actual distribution spread and the dated contract, carries 100% [S3, S4, F68].
